sections.title: Equipment
sections.note: Swords, shields, mail and gloves are one row each; tap the row for the next upgrade.

items.name: Sword
items.notes: Zelda Wiki calls the Tempered and Golden Swords the Master Sword Lv2 and Lv3. On the SNES only the Golden Sword can hurt Ganon without a Spin Attack; on the GBA the Tempered Sword can too, and the Golden Sword also breaks pots there.

tiers.name: Fighter's Sword
tiers.howTo: From your uncle in the secret passage under Hyrule Castle.

tiers.name: Master Sword
tiers.howTo: Draw it from the pedestal in the Lost Woods once you have the three Pendants.

tiers.name: Tempered Sword
tiers.howTo: In the Dark World, lift the dark rock south of the Village of Outcasts with the Titan's Mitt and talk to the frog trapped there: he is the lost dwarven swordsmith. Use the Magic Mirror where the Smithy stands to bring him to his partner east of Kakariko. Pay 10 Rupees, leave the Master Sword with them, go one screen away and come back for it.

tiers.name: Golden Sword
tiers.howTo: Throw the Tempered Sword into the Fat Fairy's pond inside the Pyramid of Power, opened with the Super Bomb (see Upgrades).

items.name: Shield
items.notes: The Red Shield is also called the Fire Shield; it blocks fireballs. Pikits and Like Likes can eat the first two shields. On the GBA a Like Like can eat the Mirror Shield too, and a Dark World shop sells a replacement.

tiers.name: Fighter's Shield
tiers.howTo: From your uncle, with the Fighter's Sword.

tiers.name: Red Shield
tiers.howTo: Throw the Fighter's Shield into the Waterfall of Wishing (swim up the falls north-east of Lake Hylia with Zora's Flippers) and answer honestly, or buy it at the Dark World Shield Shop for 500 Rupees (70 on the GBA).

tiers.name: Mirror Shield
tiers.howTo: In the Big Chest of Turtle Rock.

items.name: Mail
items.notes: Link starts in the Green Clothes. Each mail halves the damage of the one before.

tiers.name: Blue Mail
tiers.howTo: In the Big Chest of the Ice Palace.

tiers.name: Red Mail
tiers.howTo: In the Big Chest of Ganon's Tower.

tiers.name: Power Glove
tiers.howTo: In the Big Chest of the Desert Palace. Lifts light-grey rocks.

tiers.name: Titan's Mitt
tiers.howTo: In the Big Chest of Thieves' Town. Lifts the dark rocks.

items.name: Pegasus Shoes
items.howTo: Sahasrahla gives them once you have the Pendant of Courage from the Eastern Palace.
items.notes: Dash with A on the SNES, R on the GBA. Needed for the Book of Mudora.

items.name: Zora's Flippers
items.howTo: Follow the river to the falls in the far north-east of the Light World and buy them from King Zora for 500 Rupees.
items.notes: GBA only: Link can dive while swimming.

items.name: Moon Pearl
items.howTo: In the Big Chest of the Tower of Hera. Keeps Link from turning into a rabbit in the Dark World.

sections.title: Items
sections.note: Everything on the item screen apart from Bottles.

items.name: Bow
items.notes: Ganon can only be finished with Silver Arrows.

tiers.name: Bow
tiers.howTo: In the Big Chest of the Eastern Palace.

tiers.name: Silver Arrows
tiers.howTo: Throw the Bow into the Fat Fairy's pond inside the Pyramid of Power, opened with the Super Bomb.

tiers.name: Boomerang
tiers.howTo: In a chest in the Hyrule Castle dungeon, before Zelda's cell.

tiers.name: Magical Boomerang
tiers.howTo: Throw the Boomerang into the Waterfall of Wishing and answer honestly.

items.name: Hookshot
items.howTo: In the Big Chest of the Swamp Palace.

items.name: Mushroom & Magic Powder
items.notes: On the GBA the assistant is Maple. The powder wakes the Mad Batter (see Upgrades).

tiers.name: Mushroom
tiers.howTo: In a clearing in the north of the Lost Woods.

tiers.name: Magic Powder
tiers.howTo: Give the Mushroom to the witch outside the Magic Shop, by the river in the north-east of the Light World. Leave the area and come back: her assistant inside hands over the powder.

items.name: Fire Rod
items.howTo: In the Big Chest of Skull Woods.

items.name: Ice Rod
items.area: Ice Rod Cave (east of Lake Hylia)
items.howTo: Bomb the cracked wall of the cave on the east shore of Lake Hylia and open the chest inside.
items.notes: Needed, with the Fire Rod, for Trinexx in Turtle Rock. StrategyWiki puts the cave in the lake's north-east corner.

items.name: Bombos Medallion
items.howTo: In the Dark World, use the Magic Mirror from the patch of ground at the east end of the canyon by the swamp to land on the clifftop at the edge of the Desert of Mystery. Read the tablet with the Book of Mudora and raise the Master Sword.
items.notes: The only medallion the story never needs. StrategyWiki gives the Dark World spot as the east end of the canyon; Zelda Wiki and Zelda Dungeon say only "near the swamp".

items.name: Ether Medallion
items.howTo: Cross the bridge west of the Tower of Hera, read the tablet with the Book of Mudora and raise the Master Sword.
items.notes: Opens Misery Mire.

items.name: Quake Medallion
items.howTo: In the north-east of the Dark World, north of the Palace of Darkness, throw something into the ring of stones in the lake to wake the Catfish, who gives you the medallion to be left alone.
items.notes: Opens Turtle Rock. What to throw: a rock (Zelda Dungeon), a skull (Zelda Wiki) or the sign (StrategyWiki).

items.name: Lamp
items.howTo: In the chest in Link's House at the start. If you leave it, it's in a chest in Hyrule Castle instead.
items.notes: GBA only: the Lamp's flame hurts enemies.

items.name: Magic Hammer
items.howTo: In the Big Chest of the Palace of Darkness.

items.name: Shovel & Flute
items.notes: The man in the Kakariko tavern tells you about the weathercock. On the SNES the Flute takes the Shovel's slot; on the GBA the Shovel keeps its own.

tiers.name: Shovel
tiers.howTo: Talk to the boy playing the flute in the Dark World's Haunted Grove, south of the Village of Outcasts.

tiers.name: Flute
tiers.howTo: Dig in the Light World's Haunted Grove, south of Kakariko, to find the boy's Flute, and play it for him in the Dark World.

tiers.name: Bird freed
tiers.howTo: Play the Flute at the weathercock in the middle of Kakariko Village to free the bird, which then flies you to eight places in the Light World.

items.name: Bug-Catching Net
items.howTo: Talk to the sick boy in bed in Kakariko Village while you have a Bottle.
items.notes: Catches bees and fairies for Bottles, and hits Agahnim's magic back.

items.name: Book of Mudora
items.howTo: Dash into the top of the bookshelf with the Pegasus Shoes to knock the book down.
items.notes: Reads Hylian: opens the Desert Palace and gives the Bombos and Ether Medallions.

items.name: Cane of Somaria
items.howTo: In the Big Chest of Misery Mire.

items.name: Cane of Byrna
items.howTo: Drop from the ledge south of the warp tile below Ganon's Tower into the cave. Pound the moles with the Magic Hammer, cross the spikes with the Magic Cape (or with plenty of hearts and a fairy in a Bottle) and lift the rock in front of the chest with the Power Glove.
items.notes: Optional: the story never needs it.

items.name: Magic Cape
items.howTo: Lift the dark rocks around the grave at the top right of the Graveyard with the Titan's Mitt (or use the Magic Mirror from the Dark World to land inside them), then dash into the gravestone with the Pegasus Shoes.

items.name: Magic Mirror
items.howTo: Lift the rock at the foot of Death Mountain, north-east of Kakariko, with the Power Glove and climb through the dark cave, where the Lost Old Man asks to be led home. He gives you the Mirror at his cave.
items.notes: In the Dark World it sends Link back to the same spot in the Light World.

items.name: Street merchant
items.howTo: The man at the stall in the middle of Kakariko Village sells one for 100 Rupees.

items.name: Kakariko inn
items.howTo: Go in through the inn's back door, on its north-east side, and open the chest in the small room.

items.name: Man under the bridge
items.area: Under the bridge north of Lake Hylia
items.howTo: With Zora's Flippers, swim up the river east of Link's House to the man camping under the stone bridge.

items.name: Purple chest
items.area: Dark World Smithy; Desert of Mystery
items.howTo: Once the swordsmiths are reunited, a purple chest appears in the ruined Smithy in the Dark World. It follows you but can't jump down ledges or be dashed with. Bring it through the Mirror to the man in the canyon near the Desert of Mystery, who opens it if you keep his secret.
items.notes: Zelda Dungeon says the chest appears after the Tempered Sword, StrategyWiki once the smith is back with his partner. Zelda Wiki puts the man near the entrance to the Desert of Mystery, Zelda Dungeon by the signpost west of the Great Swamp.

items.name: Half magic
items.area: Mad Batter's well (beside the Smithy, east of Kakariko)
items.howTo: Pound the peg in front of the well next to the Smithy with the Magic Hammer (or use the Mirror from the Dark World to land beside it), drop in and sprinkle Magic Powder on the altar. The Mad Batter halves how much magic your items use.
items.reward: Items use half as much magic

items.name: Bomb capacity
items.area: Pond of Happiness (island in Lake Hylia)
items.howTo: Swim to the island in the middle of Lake Hylia with Zora's Flippers and throw Rupees into the pond, 5 or 20 at a time (25 or 50 once you've met the fairy). Every 100 Rupees, the fairy Venus asks whether to raise your bomb or arrow capacity.
items.notes: 100 Rupees an upgrade: 1,400 for all fourteen bombs and arrows (StrategyWiki). Not needed for speedrun.com's 100% categories. Zelda Wiki's bomb table lists only 25, 30, 35, 40 and 50.

items.name: Arrow capacity
items.area: Pond of Happiness (island in Lake Hylia)
items.howTo: Swim to the island in the middle of Lake Hylia with Zora's Flippers and throw Rupees into the pond, 5 or 20 at a time (25 or 50 once you've met the fairy). Every 100 Rupees, the fairy Venus asks whether to raise your bomb or arrow capacity.
items.notes: 100 Rupees an upgrade: 1,400 for all fourteen bombs and arrows (StrategyWiki). Not needed for speedrun.com's 100% categories. Zelda Wiki's bomb table lists only 25, 30, 35, 40 and 50.
